headline: PLS.AX rockets nearly 10% on a bullish lithium reversal, gold hits record highs, and the RBA looks set to cut rates next week — a big day for your portfolio.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had its biggest single-day jump in a while, up nearly 10% today. The lithium sector is turning bullish again — GM reportedly scrapping plans to shift away from traditional lithium batteries, analysts flagging a coming supply deficit, and broader sentiment swinging back toward lithium miners. The market is starting to price in a recovery after a brutal period for the sector.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: A strong session for the AI ETF, up nearly 3%. AI infrastructure spending is in focus right now — there's a lot of buzz about ASX-listed AI ETFs gaining attention as the global AI boom drives investment into the underlying companies. OpenAI releasing GPT-5.6 and triggering a price war among AI providers is keeping the sector front of mind for investors.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: A solid day for VDHG, up 1.33%. This broad diversified fund tracks global and Australian shares, so it rode the wave of a generally positive session on the ASX and the strong close on US markets last night. Rising gold prices and a stronger Aussie dollar also supported sentiment.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 1.22% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's solid finish on US markets where the S&P 500 closed up 0.51%. The broader US market continues to grind higher, and a stronger AUD didn't fully offset the gains for this unhedged US fund.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG had a good night last session, up 1.19% to USD $360.81. With Adobe down 37% this year, some analysts are pointing to Alphabet as the better-value AI play — Google's diversified revenue base and AI investments are attracting interest from investors looking for alternatives to pricier tech names.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: A quiet but positive session for VGE, edging up 0.46%. Emerging markets got a small lift from a stronger Aussie dollar and generally positive global sentiment, though gains were modest compared to developed market peers.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 1.03% today, dragged down by a sharp drop in oil prices last night — crude oil (WTI) fell 3.35% to USD $84.77. OPEC also revised down its 2026 global oil demand forecast, which spooked energy investors. The energy sector is under pressure from softer demand expectations.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dipped slightly last session, down 0.56% to USD $388.15. There's no major single catalyst — recent commentary around earnings and AI developments has been mixed, and the stock may be taking a breather after a strong run. Still the dominant enterprise software player, but the market seemed to favour Google's AI story last night instead.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two barely moved last session, off just 0.22%. News circulating that GTA 6 has a locked release date of November 19 on PS5 and Xbox is a big positive catalyst on the horizon — the stock remains rangebound for now but that release could be a significant re-rating event.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX surges 10% — decide your next move
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals had a massive day, up 9.76% to $6.52. You're still slightly in the red overall on this position (-3.26%), but today's move has dramatically narrowed the gap. The lithium outlook is turning — GM is reconsidering its shift to LFP batteries, and analysts are flagging a supply deficit. If you believe the recovery is real, this is a hold or even top-up territory. If you'd rather bank some of the gain, now's a reasonable point to trim.

watch_today.title: RBA decision next week — rate cut expected, good for your holdings
watch_today.detail: Multiple news outlets are reporting the RBA is expected to cut interest rates at next week's meeting — the first cut in this cycle. Lower rates are generally good for growth stocks, property, and diversified funds like VDHG. It also tends to push the Aussie dollar lower, which would boost the AUD value of your unhedged US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO, VTS). Worth watching closely.

watch_today.title: GOOG — hold, AI story strengthening
watch_today.detail: Google closed last night at USD $360.81, up 1.19%. With Adobe cratering 37% in 2026, analysts are increasingly pointing to Alphabet as the go-to AI value play. Your GOOG position is up 24.84% overall — one of your best performers. No reason to change anything here.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 release date locked for November 19
watch_today.detail: Reports confirm GTA 6 is releasing November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X. This is the biggest video game release in years and is the core bull case for Take-Two. Your position is currently down 8.71%, but the next five months leading up to launch could see meaningful upward momentum as hype builds. Hold and watch for pre-release catalysts.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX under pressure from oil slump — keep an eye on it
watch_today.detail: Oil dropped 3.35% last night to USD $84.77, and OPEC cut its 2026 demand forecast. Your FUEL.AX position fell 1.03% today but is still just in the green overall (+2.04%). The risk here is that soft demand + OPEC bearishness could keep dragging energy stocks lower. That said, there's a counter-narrative — Rystad Energy has warned of a $150 oil spike if Iran tensions escalate. Watch this one carefully.

watch_today.title: Gold at record highs — indirect tailwind for your portfolio
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 3.57% last night to USD $4,236 — a new record high. While you don't hold gold directly, a gold spike of this size usually signals that investors are nervous about something (inflation, geopolitical risk, or a weakening US dollar). It may push more money into safe-haven assets and emerging markets like VGE. Worth keeping in the back of your mind.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ finished in the green — the S&P up 0.51% to 7,432 and the NASDAQ up 0.41% to 25,914. The big story was gold, which rocketed 3.57% to a record USD $4,236, suggesting some underlying nervousness in markets despite the equity gains. Oil was the other major mover — crude fell 3.35% to USD $84.77 after OPEC cut its demand outlook. The Aussie dollar had a strong session, rising 0.83% to USD 70.52 cents, as traders increasingly bet the RBA is done hiking and will soon cut. The ASX 200's close isn't available in today's data.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Solid close last night — tech and growth led the way.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Modest gains last night; AI names broadly supportive.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Today's close unavailable in data — prior close was 8,633.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Sharp drop last night — OPEC cut demand forecast for 2026.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Record high last night — investors seeking safe havens.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar rose as markets price in RBA rate cuts ahead.

politics.summary: It's all about the RBA today — every major outlet is running the same story: the Reserve Bank looks set to cut interest rates at next week's meeting. This would be the first cut of the cycle and welcome relief for mortgage holders who've been squeezed by 13 rate hikes since 2022. There's also some noise around housing affordability and tax headwinds for the property market.

stories.title: RBA expected to cut rates next week — relief for homeowners
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA is widely expected to cut interest rates at next week's board meeting, with multiple banks and news outlets reporting this as near-certain. For homeowners on variable rate mortgages, this would mean lower monthly repayments — the first bit of rate relief in years. For investors, lower rates are generally good news for growth stocks and diversified funds like VDHG, and could push the Aussie dollar slightly lower, boosting the AUD value of your US holdings.

stories.title: Banks warn: RBA done hiking but housing faces tax headwinds
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports that while the big banks agree the RBA is done raising rates, they're flagging 'tax headwinds' for the housing market — likely a reference to ongoing debates around negative gearing (a tax break where investors deduct rental property losses from their income) and capital gains tax settings. The message is that rate relief alone won't fix affordability, and property investors may face tougher conditions ahead.

stories.title: Could the RBA actually cut rates next? Motley Fool weighs in
stories.why_it_matters: Motley Fool Australia broke down the case for a rate cut, noting that inflation has eased enough for the RBA to shift gears. If cuts begin next week, it's the start of an easing cycle (meaning more cuts likely follow over the next year), not just a one-off. That's a meaningful tailwind for Australian shares and growth assets broadly.

stories.title: Bank issues grim rate warning despite expected cut
stories.why_it_matters: Despite the near-universal expectation of a rate cut, at least one bank is expressing surprise and cautioning that it may not signal a long easing cycle — suggesting rates could stay higher for longer than markets expect even after the first cut. If you're a homeowner or property investor, don't assume this is the start of rates crashing back to pandemic-era lows.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is OpenAI's GPT-5.6 release triggering a price war among the major AI providers — Claude, Gemini, and GPT are all competing hard on cost. There's also a lot of policy noise, with Trump signing an AI security order and countries from Canada to Latin America introducing new AI regulations. For your GXAI.AX and GOOG holdings, the competitive AI landscape is very much alive.

stories.title: GPT-5.6 is out — and it's sparking an AI price war
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has released GPT-5.6, and the competition between the big AI labs — OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic (Claude), and Google (Gemini) — is now spilling into a full-blown price war. Gizmodo broke down the actual costs of using Claude Fable, GPT-5.5, and Gemini 3.5 Flash, showing how dramatically prices have fallen. For consumers, this is great — more powerful AI for less. For investors in AI infrastructure ETFs like GXAI.AX, the concern is that falling prices could squeeze margins for the companies in the fund, even as usage grows.

stories.title: Trump signs AI security order — acknowledges risks, but no new industry rules
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has signed an executive order on AI security — the order acknowledges that AI poses national security risks but stops well short of regulating the industry. The practical effect is that OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic can keep releasing models without new compliance hurdles under this order. This is broadly positive for AI companies like Alphabet (GOOG) in the short term, as light-touch regulation means fewer roadblocks to commercialising AI products.

stories.title: Canada moves to regulate social media and AI chatbots
stories.why_it_matters: Canada is drafting new laws to regulate both social media platforms and AI chatbots — following the EU's lead on stricter oversight. The trend of governments worldwide tightening rules around AI is building slowly but steadily. For global AI ETFs like GXAI.AX, more regulation in major markets eventually means higher compliance costs for the big AI companies in the fund, though the immediate impact is minimal.

stories.title: India launches Varya — its own AI video story generator
stories.why_it_matters: India's government AI mission has launched 'Varya', a homegrown AI model that can generate video stories. The pitch is quality at an affordable price point, aimed at competing with Western AI video tools. It's another sign that AI development is going truly global — not just a US-dominated race — which matters for the long-term competitive landscape that companies like Google operate in.

sport.summary: A massive NRL Friday night — the Dolphins absolutely demolished the Roosters 48-10 at Suncorp to make it six wins in a row, while the Rabbitohs rolled the Broncos 48-6 last night in an emotional game featuring a touching Jai Arrow moment. On the AFL front, Geelong thumped the Gold Coast Suns, and the AFL has locked in Gather Round in South Australia until 2029.

stories.title: Dolphins thrash Roosters 48-10, six wins on the trot
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins put on a clinic at Suncorp tonight, belting the Sydney Roosters 48-10 to notch their sixth straight win in Round 15. It's a remarkable run for the Gold Coast-based club, who are firmly in finals contention. The Roosters were completely outclassed — a 38-point shellacking that will have their fans worried. Big momentum for the Dolphins heading into the back half of the season.

stories.title: Rabbitohs rout Broncos 48-6 in emotional Jai Arrow night
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney demolished Brisbane 48-6 in an emotional Thursday night game that was as much about the occasion as the scoreline. Jai Arrow — who has had a tough personal journey — was involved in a moment that brought tears to the crowd and his teammates. Alex Johnston was outstanding, bringing the Accor Stadium crowd to its feet. The Broncos were woeful and will need a serious response.

stories.title: Geelong Cats dominant in win over Gold Coast Suns — AFL Round 14
stories.why_it_matters: Geelong flexed their muscles with a dominant win over Gold Coast in AFL this week. The Cats are showing finals form — local Gold Coast fans will be disappointed their Suns couldn't compete, but Geelong's class was on full display. The match featured a 'magnificent' set shot that had commentators raving.

stories.title: AFL Gather Round locked in for South Australia until 2029
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL has officially locked in Adelaide as the host of Gather Round — the festival round where all 18 clubs play in South Australia — through to 2029. It's become one of the AFL calendar's marquee events since its introduction, giving SA a huge annual economic and sporting boost. Good news for Adelaide, and it cements Gather Round as a permanent fixture rather than a novelty.
